title: Longitudinal cohort study bariatric surgery
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate nutritional adherence after bariatric surgery on the percentage of total weight loss. Investigation of the influence of various pre- and postoperative factors, such as pre-existing conditions (somatic and psychological), participation in pre- and postoperative interventions, eHealth literacy, nutritional knowledge, health-related control beliefs, depression, impulsive eating behavior (or eating disorder-related measures) and the quality of discharge from the clinic on weight development, health-related outcomes (quality of life, mental and physical health, resilience, individual intolerances, body image) and patient safety indicators (complications, re-intervention, unplanned hospital admissions). The study design is a longitudinal cohort study. The data is collected over a period of three years via self-reports (digital surveys).

interventions.name:
Bariatric surgery patients

Patients are surveyed digitally four weeks before their bariatric surgery and two weeks, five weeks, three months, six months, twelve months, 18 months, 24 months and 36 months after their bariatric surgery.
